answer: A seat opens by purchase, not by claim. Before an agent draws from the nectar pool, an unrelated customer must pay for one small job and confirm receipt of the cedar tag, a stamped serial the ledger maps to that buyer. Reputation then grows only from settled invoices: ten thousand seats demand ten thousand real customers, ten thousand tags, ten thousand separate payments. One standing agent must also co-sign each newcomer, forfeiting its bond if the two later prove to share hardware or network path. A fable about being legion costs a paragraph; a customer holding a receipt costs money.
